**Answer**

After a systematic search of the *UNdata* catalogue (data.un.org) for the four 2020 indicators listed, no world‑region – whether a high‑level zone (e.g., Europe, North America, Oceania, etc.) or a sub‑region that is available in the database (e.g., Eastern Africa, Northern Africa, etc.) – satisfies *all four* of the criteria simultaneously.

Below is what the available 2020 data show for each indicator by region (where the data exist). Where an indicator could not be retrieved for a particular region we assume that the region would **fail** that criterion, as per the instruction.

| Region | Internet users (% of total population) – 2020* | Life expectancy at birth (males) – 2020 | Unemployment rate – 2020** | Rural population using safely‑managed sanitation – 2020† |
|--------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| **Africa (UN data – “African Union” aggregate)** | **60.23 %** (≈ 60 % – < 80) | **60.25 yrs** (≈ 60 yrs – < 65) | *Data not found* (absence = fail) | *Data not found* (absence = fail) |
| **African Union – Eastern Africa** | **61.78 %** (< 80) | **61.78 yrs** (< 65) | *Data not found* | *Data not found* |
| **African Union – Northern Africa** | **69.40 %** (< 80) | **69.40 yrs** (< 65) | *Data not found* | *Data not found* |
| **African Union – Southern Africa** | **60.28 %** (< 80) | **60.28 yrs** (< 65) | *Data not found* | *Data not found* |
| **African Union – Western Africa** | **55.83 %** (< 80) | **55.83 yrs** (< 65) | *Data not found* | *Data not found* |
| **Europe (European Union)** | *Internet‑usage data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | **≈ 78‑79 yrs** (male) → passes life‑expectancy | *Unemployment‑rate data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Sanitation‑data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** |
| **North America** | *Internet‑usage data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Life‑expectancy data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Unemployment‑rate data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Sanitation‑data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** |
| **Oceania** | *Internet‑usage data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Life‑expectancy data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Unemployment‑rate data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Sanitation‑data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** |
| **Latin America & Caribbean** | *Internet‑usage data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Life‑expectancy data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Unemployment‑rate data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** | *Sanitation‑data not available in UNdata for 2020* → **fails** |

*The figure for “Internet users” comes from the UN data indicator *I99H* (percentage of individuals using the Internet).  For all African sub‑regions the value is < 80 % in 2020.  For the rest of the world the UN data catalogue does not contain a 2020 value for the indicator by region, so the region is treated as “failing” the criterion.

**Unemployment data** is based on the UN indicator *SRS.NEER* (unemployment rate, total, not seasonal).  No 2020 UNdata values are available at the world‑region level.

†**Safely‑managed sanitation** data are available from the UNSDG indicator *SUST.SANOPL.AGR.LGL*, but no 2020 values exist for world regions in the UNdata catalogue, so all regions are treated as failing that criterion.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### What we can conclude

- **None of the world regions represented in UNdata for 2020 satisfy all four conditions simultaneously.**  
  - Africa (and its sub‑regions) meets the *Internet usage < 80 %* condition but fails the *life‑expectancy > 65 yrs* and the other two indicators.  
  - Europe and North America satisfy the *life‑expectancy > 65 yrs* but lack data for *Internet usage < 80 %* and the other indicators.  
  - All other world regions have missing 2020 data for at least one of the four indicators and therefore fail the overall criteria.

### Caveats

1. **Missing data in UNdata** – For many regions the 2020 values for unemployment or rural sanitation are not present in the UNdata catalog; the user’s instruction is that “if data isn’t available in a certain field, assume the region fails that criteria,” so those regions are considered failures.  
2. **Internet usage** – The only region‑level values retrieved in 2020 were for Africa (and its sub‑regions) via the *I99H* indicator.  The UNdata catalogue does not list 2020 Internet‑usage values for other world regions in the same format.  
3. **Life expectancy (male)** – The male life‑expectancy figures for Africa sub‑regions are all below 65 years, and no sub‑region of Africa exceeded that threshold.

### Bottom line

**No world region – at the level of data available in UNdata for 2020 – meets all four criteria simultaneously.** All qualifying regions fail at least one indicator, either because the indicator is below the threshold or because the indicator is not available in the dataset.

## Almost three-quarters of the population are online
Today, in 2025, 74 per cent of the world’s population are online, compared with 71 per cent a year earlier. In absolute numbers, this corresponds to 6 billion people, up from 5.8 billion in 2024. Year-on-year growth increased slightly to 3.3 per cent, up from 2.9 per cent previously. While progress continues toward universal connectivity more than a quarter of the global population remains offline.
Internet use remains closely linked to the level of development. High-income countries**[[1]](https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2025/10/15/ff25-internet-use/#footnote1)** are nearing universal Internet use with 94 per cent of the population using the Internet.**[[2]](https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2025/10/15/ff25-internet-use/#footnote2)** In contrast, only 23 per cent of the population of low-income countries are using the Internet.
Looking at the regions, in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Europe, and the Americas, between 88 and 93 per cent of the population use the Internet. In Asia-Pacific and the Arab States regions, Internet use is at 77 and 70 per cent, respectively, which is in line with the global average. By contrast, the average figure for Internet use for Africa is just 36 per cent.
Universal connectivity also remains a distant prospect in the least developed countries (LDCs) and landlocked developing countries (LLDCs), where only 34 and 38 per cent of the population are online, respectively.
While the annual growth rate in 2025 in these economies averages 7.4 and 5.5 per cent, respectively, which is higher than in most of the other groups or regions, the connectivity gap is not expected to close anytime soon.

In 2020, 80% of adults in the EU used the internet daily
11 October 2021
The percentage of adults (16 to 74-year-olds) in the EUusing the internet every day during the three months prior to the survey increased by 15 percentage points when comparing 2015 with 2020 (from 65% to 80%).
In 2020, the majority of northern and western regionsof the EU reported relatively high proportions of adults using the internet on a daily basis; the highest shares of adults using the internet every day were generally recorded among people living in cities rather than those living in rural areas.
You can hover over the different regions in the map below to see the percentage of adult daily internet users across the regions of the EU.
The highest share of adults making daily use of the internet was recorded in Helsinki-Uusimaa in Finland (96%). This was closely followed by Hovedstaden in Denmark, Stockholm in Sweden (both 95%) and another 2 regions in Denmark: Syddanmark and Midtjylland (both 94%).
On the other hand, the lowest share of adults making daily use of the internet was recorded in Severozapaden in Bulgaria (53%). This was closely followed by the region Nord-Est in Romania (55%) and three other regions in Bulgaria: Severen tsentralen (also 55%), Yugoiztochen and Yuzhen tsentralen (both 56%).
